comparator.route: Broad psychology route combining Cognitive Neuroscience and Social Psychology in Organisations
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 prospectus and current programme structure establish a broad three-year Psychology bachelor covering the major subdisciplines, methods and statistics, professional skills, specialisation choice, electives and a 15-EC bachelor project. The adopted 2025–2026 OER supplies the component-level credit structure that the current pages continue to describe: 60 EC first year, 60 EC later compulsory work, at least 20 EC of specialisation courses, 10 EC of Psychology electives and 30 EC of free-choice space. This coherent broad pathway instantiates Cognitive Neuroscience and Social Psychology in Organisations as two contrasting specialisation courses rather than selecting a narrow single-domain profile; the Psychology-elective and free-choice spaces remain open.

alternatives.label: Closest match to Psychology
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible psychology programme combining social, developmental, clinical, cognitive and organisational psychology with statistics, research methods, assessment-related study and cross-disciplinary perspectives on behaviour.
progression: The sociology sequence progresses from Introduction through Modern Sociology to Contemporary Social Theory; advanced psychology follows the psychology gateway and statistics.

alternatives.label: Brain & cognition
alternatives.concept: A Brain and Cognition route centred on cognitive neuroscience, perception, higher-order functions, language, biological foundations and quantitative/data-oriented research.
alternatives.distinctness: Neuroscience, life and health sciences, anatomy, physiology and data replace part of the broad psychology mix.
progression: Life-science foundations precede physiology, anatomy and laboratory work, then disease and pathology; cognition, psychology and data courses build from earlier gateways and methods, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Psychology, leadership & organisations
alternatives.concept: A Work and Organisational Psychology route centred on organisational behaviour, leadership, diversity, negotiation, workplace wellbeing, behavioural decision-making and applied organisational research.
alternatives.labelReason: The broader label reflects the completed mix of psychology, leadership, organisations, sociology, communication, business and behavioural economics.
alternatives.distinctness: Organisational psychology and leadership replace the biological and cognitive emphasis.
progression: Psychology, business, sociology, methods and leadership foundations precede advanced organisational, communication and behavioural courses.

routeSelection.route: Broad psychology route combining Cognitive Neuroscience and Social Psychology in Organisations
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Psychology bachelor. The programme requires specialisation choices but is explicitly broad. Selecting one cognitive-neuroscience course and one social-organisational course preserves that cross-domain identity and avoids presenting a narrow clinical, cognitive or organisational profile as the whole programme. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme-wide psychology and research core. Brain and cognition and social and organisational psychology are independently evidenced, coherent, mechanically feasible and substantively distinct additional routes. Clinical/mental-health and development/trauma directions were also assessed, but three UCR alternatives is the maximum.

blocks: Brain and Perception substantially corresponds to UCR Perception & Action, which examines neural mechanisms of perception and action; the comparator was placed only after the canonical UCR rows were fixed.

notes.text: Leiden Psychology provides a structured disciplinary sequence with dedicated psychometrics, psychodiagnostics, professional skills, specialisation courses and a supervised 15-EC bachelor project. UCR can build substantial psychology, cognition and organisational programmes, but it does not reproduce the same specialist practical structure or professional-qualification pathway.
